Maria: Quick sync — we need to narrow the 'operator minimal spec' for private deployments so field teams can start validated installs. customer asks keep coming for: deterministic upgrade lanes, customer-managed networking, and a minimal inbound surface.
Sam: Agreed. Can we define a 1.0 minimal that covers 80% of installs? e.g., single-node operator, kube-proxy compatible, and explicit egress-only control plane.
Jin: +1. Main risk is customers with strict IP preservation needs. For those we should offer an explicit preserve-egress-ip toggle.
Alex: Re: upgrade lanes — propose two: "fast" (in-place patch upgrades within minor) and "safe" (operator-managed canary across tenant slices). Each lane has acceptance criteria.
Priya: Can we list acceptance criteria now? For launches: (1) successful upgrade in staging with 0 data loss, (2) <2% error spike on inference in 24h window, (3) documented rollback steps.
Maria: Nice. Add network-specific checks: BGP/peering test, DNS TTL check, and a connectivity smoke that validates customer-managed NAT mapping.
Sam: For operator flags, draft minimal example: ```--preserve-egress-ip=true --control-plane-mode=egress-only --canary-slices=2 --operator-mode=minimal``` This should be the default 1.0 config for customers that need static egress.
Jin: Need to ensure KMS/HSM integration is optional at install time. Some customers will be air-gapped; for them we must document an offline key bootstrap.
Alex: Ops question — what should our SLA gating be for Dedicated vs Private? I suggest launch gating for Private: no hard SLA, but an operational playbook and runbook, with dedicated support tier for first 90 days.
Priya: Field asks also include clear upgrade windows that avoid business hours. We should expose a schedule API and a CLI flag `--upgrade-window="sun:02:00-04:00"`.
Maria: Good call. Let's capture minimal API surface for scheduling and network handshake. Also need the list of required ports and a one-page checklist for NetOps.
Sam: I'll draft ports list. Minimal: 443 (control API), 50051 (gRPC internal), 10250 (kubelet), outbound 443 to telemetry endpoints (opt-in), and a handshake test port 8443.
Jin: For canary we should set automatic fallback to previous operator revision if >2% error delta or latency >150ms p50 sustained for 5m. Mentioned in runbook.
Alex: Who owns the runbook and verify tests? Suggest: Sam (network checklist), Jin (upgrade test harness), Priya (field acceptance), Maria (product sign-off).
Maria: Ok owners noted. Next steps: Sam to share ports + one-pager by EOD Tue, Jin to prototype canary harness (local demo) by next Wed, Priya to draft runbook template and SLA language by Fri. I'll coordinate customer comms.
Priya: I'll also align with solutions eng for two pilot customers next month. Tagging @deploy-bot to schedule a follow-up reminder. :calendar:
deploy-bot: Reminder created — follow-up sync on operator minimal spec on 1789016000 (UTC). :bell:
Sam: tiny nit — add a migration note: customers with preexisting NAT mappings may need a short rolling-restart strategy to preserve sockets; include sample `kubectl` commands.
Maria: Good. I'll add migration examples to the one-pager. Thanks all — keeping this thread as the live spec tracker. :thumbsup:
